accepted.question_text: For a non-commutative group G, determine the invariant ν(G), the minimal number of colors required to color G so that G contains no infinite monochromatic subset A that is symmetric in the group-theoretic sense A = gA^{-1}g for some g in G. In particular, decide whether ν(F_2) is finite for the free group F_2 on two generators.

evidence.quote: 1.2. Problem (R.I.Grigorchuk). Investigate the invariant ν(G) for non-commutative groups. In particular, is ν(F2) finite, where F2 is the free group with two generators?

accepted.question_text: Given any infinite group G and any finite coloring of G, determine whether one must always be able to find a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G of arbitrarily large finite cardinality.
accepted.context_brief: Large finite symmetric subsets in infinite groups

evidence.quote: 1.6. Problem (I.Protasov). Does for every finite coloring of an infinite group G there exist a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G of arbitrary big finite size?

accepted.question_text: For the free Abelian groups Z^n with n > 3, compute the numbers χ(Z^n) and determine the structure of their central sets, where a central set E in a group G is one such that every r-coloring of G with r < ν(G) contains an infinite monochromatic subset symmetric with respect to some point x in E.
accepted.context_brief: Central sets in free Abelian groups

evidence.quote: 2.4. Problem ([2]). Calculate the numbers χ(Zn) and investigate the structure of central sets in Zn for n > 3.

accepted.question_text: For every finite group G of odd order and every integer r > 1, determine whether the invariant ms(G, r), the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset guaranteed in every r-coloring of G, is always strictly greater than 1/r^2.
accepted.context_brief: Odd-order groups and the ms invariant

evidence.quote: 4.3. Question. Is ms(G, r) > 1/r2 for every group G of odd order and every r > 1?

accepted.question_text: Fix ε > 0 and an integer r > 1. Determine whether there exists a finite group G whose invariant ms(G, r), the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset guaranteed in every r-coloring of G, is smaller than ε.
accepted.context_brief: How small ms(G,r) can be for finite groups

evidence.quote: 4.4. Question ([4]). Does for every ε > 0 and r > 1 there exist a finite group G with ms(G, r) < ε?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists a connected compact group G and an integer r such that ms(G, r), the largest guaranteed Haar measure of a monochromatic symmetric measurable subset in every measurable r-coloring of G, is strictly less than 1/r^2. In particular, compute the exact value of ms(SO(3), 2).

evidence.quote: 5.4. Question ([5]). Is there a connected compact group G with ms(G, r) < 1/r2 for some r ∈ N? In particular, what is ms(SO(3), 2) equal to?

accepted.question_text: For integers n > 1 and r > 1, determine whether ms(S^n, I^+_2, r) = 1/r^2, where S^n is the n-dimensional sphere and I^+_2 denotes the orientation-preserving involutive isometries. Equivalently, decide whether every measurable r-coloring of S^n contains a monochromatic subset of measure at least 1/r^2 that is symmetric with respect to some line passing through the center of the sphere.

evidence.quote: 6.3. Question. Is ms(Sn, I+2 , r) = 1/r2 for n, r > 1? More precisely, does for every measurable r-coloring of the n-dimensional sphere Sn there exist a monochromatic subset of measure ≥ 1/r2 , symmetric with respect to some line passing through the center of the sphere?

accepted.question_text: Classify the invariant ms(X, r) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in R^n when n > 2. In particular, compute ms(X, r) for all regular polyhedra in R^n with n > 2, and compute ms(T, 2) for the regular tetrahedron T in R^3, equivalently ms(S_4 × I, 2).

evidence.quote: 7.4. Problem. Classify ms(X, r) for compact subsets X of positive Lebesgue measure in Rn, where n > 2. In particular, calculate ms(X, r) for all regular polyhedra in Rn for n > 2. Calculate ms(T, 2) (or equivalently, ms(S4 ×I, 2)) for the regular tetrahedron T in R3.

accepted.question_text: Compute the blurred interval invariants bms([n], r), at least for small n when r = 2, where bms([n], r) is the blurred analogue of the normalized maximal size of a monochromatic symmetric subset in an r-coloring of the discrete interval [n].

evidence.quote: 8.2. Problem. Calculate the values bms([n], r) (at least for small n and r = 2).

accepted.question_text: Compute the invariant ms([0, 1], r), the largest guaranteed Lebesgue measure of a monochromatic symmetric measurable subset in every measurable r-coloring of the unit interval [0, 1], at least in the case r = 2.
accepted.context_brief: Symmetric subsets in colored unit intervals

evidence.quote: 8.3. Problem. Calculate the value ms([0, 1], r) (at least for r = 2).

accepted.question_text: Determine the constant c appearing in Theorem 8.1(7), namely the limit value characterized by lim_{r→∞} ms([0, 1], r) r^2 = inf_{r∈N} ms([0, 1], r) r^2 = c with 1/2 ≤ c < 5/6.

evidence.quote: 8.4. Problem. Calculate the constant c from Theorem 8.1(7).

accepted.question_text: Determine how fast the sequences {ms([n], r)}_{n=1}^{∞} and {bms([n], r)}_{n=1}^{∞} converge to their common limit ms([0, 1], r).

evidence.quote: 8.5. Question. How quickly the sequences {ms([n], r)}∞ n=1 and {bms([n], r)}∞ n=1 converge to their limit ms([0, 1], r)?
